findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects are stored without a customer-managed or KMS-enforced encryption default. This bucket receives the vendor roster object, so potentially sensitive third-party data is written unencrypted.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial export data stored without an enforced encryption default or KMS key boundary.
Versioning and access logging are configured but no server_side_encryption_configuration is present, so model artefacts are stored without an enforced encryption default.

No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined. Operational runbooks frequently contain internal hostnames, procedures and occasionally embedded credentials, and are stored here without enforced encryption.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket and no ACL is explicitly set, so there is no account- or bucket-level guardrail preventing a future public ACL or bucket policy from exposing its contents.

The private ACL is the only control preventing exposure; no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined, so a subsequent ACL or bucket policy change could make financial ledger exports publicly readable with no defence-in-depth backstop.

The audit log sink has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block. It uses the log-delivery-write ACL, and without a public access block nothing prevents a later policy change from exposing collected access logs.
No bucket policy denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so objects may be retrieved or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.
No bucket policy requires aws:SecureTransport, allowing financial ledger data to be transferred over plaintext HTTP.
Versioning is not enabled, so objects can be silently overwritten or permanently deleted with no recoverable prior version, removing an important integrity and anti-tampering control.
Versioning is not enabled on the financial ledger export bucket, so exported records can be overwritten or deleted irrecoverably, weakening data integrity and non-repudiation.

force_destroy = true on the bucket that serves as the access-log target for model_artifacts allows the entire audit trail, including all object versions, to be deleted by a single terraform destroy, defeating the tamper-evidence the log sink provides.
A vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded with no server_side_encryption argument into a bucket that has no default encryption, so likely sensitive third-party data is written to S3 in cleartext.
